title: Conversation SKU hinge modeling notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad to explore a hybrid conversation SKU that "hinges" between per-session base fees and per-token variable billing. Goal: find simple primitives that are friendly for product, predictable for finance, and easy to explain to customers while preserving incentives for cache/batching optimizations.

TL;DR hypotheses:
- Offer a small per-session anchor (covers session setup + warm KV/metadata) + per-token pricing for generation/embedding.
- Provide two session shapes: interactive (low tokens, high qps, latency-sensitive) and analytic (high tokens, lower qps). Anchor and token rates differ by shape.
- Expose a latency-subsidy credit for customers who opt into strict SLOs (pay slightly higher base but get preferential routing / reserved capacity).

Assumptions (back-of-envelope inputs):
- Infra blended token cost (after batching + cache benefits): $0.002 per 1k generated tokens at median workload. (This is approximate; peak worst-case ~ $0.01/1k for small batches without cache)
- Embedding unit cost treated separately: $0.03 per 1k vectors equivalent (placeholder).
- Typical interactive session: 250 tokens in, 350 tokens out total across session (600 tokens round-trip).
- Typical analytic session: 12k tokens generation (long summary or doc transform).
- Session orchestration overhead (API, KV hits, ephemeral state) amortized = ~ $0.005 per session without reserved capacity.

SKU primitives to play with:
- session_anchor: flat $0.02 per session (covers orchestration, tiny cache warm).
- token_rate_interactive: $0.0025 per 1k tokens (slightly above infra to cover ops + margin).
- token_rate_analytic: $0.0018 per 1k tokens (lower for bulk long runs).
- latency_slo_credit: +$0.01 per session OR +10% on token rate to guarantee routing on dedicated pool.
- reserved_throughput_tiers: commit to X GPU slots -> discounted token rates and waived anchors.

Worked examples:
1) Lightweight chat user (interactive)
- session_anchor $0.02 + 600 tokens * (0.0025/1000) = 0.02 + 0.0015 = $0.0215 per session (~2.15 cents).
- If user runs 10 sessions/day -> 21.5 cents/day -> $6.45/month.
- Infra cost ~ session_anchor portion mostly margin and ops. Unit economics: if infra true token cost is $0.002/1k -> generator cost = 0.0012/1k less; margin thin for small users but anchor captures overhead.

2) Long analytic job (12k tokens)
- session_anchor $0.02 + 12k * (0.0018/1000) = 0.02 + 0.0216 = $0.0416 (~4.16 cents).
- For 100 analytic jobs/month = $4.16/month. Much cheaper per-token because of lower rate.

3) Strict-SLO interactive customer opts into latency_slo_credit
- pay +$0.01/session -> 0.0315/session but guaranteed routing to dedicated pool and lower observed p95.
- Compare to paying for dedicated reserved capacity: if heavy scale, reserved may be more cost-effective.

Design considerations / tradeoffs:
- Anchors bias toward many short sessions (helps us capture orchestration cost). Danger: customers might game by bundling many calls into single session; need doc-level guidance and SDK defaults (session TTL, encourage reuse but charge anchor per TTL).
- Two token rates adds complexity but mirrors real infra: long jobs have better batching/kv reuse. Keep product messaging simple: "interactive" vs "bulk" mode. Switch detection: total tokens per session or explicit header from SDK.
- Latency_slo_credit simplifies enterprise upsell: small incremental per-session surcharge buys reserved routing for that session. Could be charged as a percentage surcharge instead of flat fee.

Open questions / experiments to run:
- Empirical numbers: run 2-week trace on hosted API to compute actual blended token cost per session shapes (need avg batch size, cache hit rate, kv lookup counts). Link: JIRA-PRIC-212 measurement plan.
- Where to set anchor so it meaningfully defrays orchestration but doesn’t deter lightweight consumer usage? Try A/B anchors: $0.00 / $0.01 / $0.02.
- How to model connection between SLO credit and true marginal cost of guaranteed capacity? We need modeling that maps credit revenue to reserved GPU hours consumed.
- Interaction with free credits and startup onboarding: consider first N sessions free OR first $X of anchors waived.

Packaging sketches (short):
- Freemium: 1000 free tokens/month + 5 free sessions (anchors waived).
- Starter: $9/mo -> 6000 tokens + 300 sessions (anchors included in plan; per-token charges afterwards at interactive rate).
- Scale: $299/mo -> 50M tokens included or heavy discount on tokens; reserved-slot add-on for p95 SLO.
- Enterprise: committed reserved capacity with committed monthly anchors waived, custom token rates, SLO credits included.

Risk notes:
- Complexity creep: too many small modifiers (anchor, slo-credit, two token rates) -> support friction. Aim to expose only 2–3 primitives to customers.
- Behavioral changes: anchors penalize extremely short ephemeral calls (e.g., single-shot embedding calls) — ensure embeddings are billed differently or exempt.

Implementation quick wins:
- Add session-type header in SDK and provisional server-side rule to apply token-rate bucket. Default to interactive unless session.reported_tokens > 5k.
- Track session-level telemetry: total_tokens_in, total_tokens_out, cache_hit_ratio, batch_size, observed_latency_p50/p95. Use these to feed pricing telemetry.
- Simple A/B experiment: enable $0.01 anchor for 10% new signups and measure retention and usage vs control.

Next steps for me:
- Ask infra for 14-day traces (JIRA-PRIC-212).
- Draft short customer-facing explanation of session anchor and the two token bands for FAQ.
- Run quick calc for margin sensitivity to anchor levels (0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05).

Random scribbles and constraints:
- Consider per-tenant monthly floor: protect us from open-source scraping with tiny calls. E.g., minimum monthly charge $1 for active tenants.
- Could consider token-bucket prepay packs that replenish anchors instead of per-session anchors for heavy users.
- For Dedicated customers, anchor should be zero and token rates discounted; anchor only for hosted tiers.

Notes-to-self: keep this intentionally opinionated but simple. One-page customer explainer + 2 internal graphs (session distribution, token-per-session CDF) should be sufficient to iterate with finance.

End of scratchpad.
